transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um, I hope I'm in the right place. I'm really just here because my manager at the restaurant got a little... concerned, I guess? It's honestly not a huge deal, and I really don't want to waste your time. 

I've just been having some little mix-ups at work. I always try to be a really good employee, but... well, I guess what scared everyone is that I started kind of freezing up in the middle of service. Or doing things out of order. Like, the other day they found me just standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and I was just repeating table numbers to myself instead of actually closing out the checks. 

I know it sounds a little strange, and I'm really embarrassed to even admit it. Am I explaining that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed any times when you couldn't remember what happened during these episodes at work, or have you experienced any memory gaps in general?

Oh, um, no... I don't think so. I actually remember everything when it happens. It's not like I black out or anything scary like that, I promise. 

Like with the cash drawer key... I knew I was standing there, and I remember exactly what I was doing, saying the numbers out loud. It was just... I just couldn't seem to make myself do the next step, if that makes sense? But my memory of it is totally fine. I don't have any gaps or lost time or anything. 

I hope that's a good sign? Does that make sense, how I'm explaining it? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
Have you ever felt like you're seeing, hearing, or sensing things that others don't, or believing things that you know other people might not agree with?

Um... well... I guess, um... I really don't want you to think I'm crazy or anything. It's probably just from being tired after a long shift, honestly. 

But, um, sometimes... like if I'm doing the closing shift at the restaurant, or even just when I'm at home in my own kitchen... I do hear this woman's voice. It's nothing scary, I promise! She just... she'll say my name. Or, like, if I'm doing the till, she'll tell me I'm doing the count wrong. 

It's just that it sounds so clear that I'll actually answer her out loud, and then a second later I realize that... well, that nobody else heard it, or that I'm actually alone. 

I hope that doesn't sound too weird? I know it's probably just stress playing tricks on my ears when I'm overworked. Is... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Can you tell me more about how often you hear that voice and how long each time usually lasts?

Um, let me think... I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is. It's honestly not that often. Maybe... I don't know, maybe a few times a week? Mostly just when it's super busy or I'm exhausted. 

And it's really quick, I promise. Just a passing thing. Like, she'll just say my name or make a quick comment about the till, and then it's over in just a few seconds. It doesn't last long at all, just a quick sentence and then she's gone. 

It's really not disrupting my life or anything, just a little blip. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining the frequency okay for you. I just don't want you to worry that it's this constant, overwhelming thing, because it's really not.
Do these episodes or the voice you hear ever cause you any distress, or make it hard for you to do things at work or in your daily life?

Um... well... I mean, I really try not to let it bother me. I want to be a good employee, you know? I try so hard to just push through it. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... it has been a little tough lately. I really don't want to complain, but... my manager did pull me aside the other day. I was up for the shift-lead position, which I was so excited about, but... well, he said I've been making too many mistakes during service, and that my confusion during closing is slowing everyone down. So... I think I might lose that opportunity. Which is fine! I mean, I understand why he's worried. 

And, um... at home... my husband... he's been so patient, he really is wonderful. But he did mention that I seem like I'm barely there lately. Like I'm just not present with him anymore. 

I'm really trying to fix it, though! I promise I'm working on being more focused. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible employee or a bad wife... I just want to be honest with you so you can help me. Is... is that the kind of information you needed?
Have you ever found yourself believing something very strongly—like thinking someone is out to get you, or that you’ve done something terrible, even if others tell you otherwise?

Um... well, I definitely don't think I've done anything terrible! I always try to be a really good person, I promise. And I wouldn't say anyone is, like, out to get me in a scary movie kind of way... I know how bad that sounds, and I really don't want you to think I'm paranoid or anything. 

But... I guess... well, since you asked... sometimes at the restaurant, I just get this really, really strong feeling that a couple of the other servers are watching me. Them, and actually one of our regular customers, too. It just feels like they're staring at me whenever I'm at the computer, watching exactly how I ring things in. 

And... um, I've been noticing these little signs on the order tickets. Like little marks or ways things are written, and it really feels like they're doing it on purpose to prove I'm making mistakes, just to get me fired. 

My husband says I'm totally overthinking it, though. He says it's just normal restaurant mess-ups and messy handwriting, and he's probably right! I know I'm probably just being insecure because of the whole shift-lead situation, so I really try to just smile and ignore it. I hope that doesn't make me sound awful or overly suspicious of people... is that the kind of thing you meant? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.

Can you tell me more about those signs you mentioned on the order tickets? Specifically, do you believe these marks or handwriting styles are intentionally placed as part of a deliberate effort to get you fired, and how strongly do you believe this?

Um... well, I know it sounds really silly when I say it out loud. I really don't want you to think I'm, you know, losing my mind or being a difficult person. But... yes, to be completely honest, I guess I do believe it pretty strongly. 

When I'm at the computer, I just keep feeling like those couple of servers and that one regular customer are watching exactly how I ring things in. And then I look at the order tickets, and it's like... the way they loop certain letters or leave these specific little marks... it just feels so obvious to me that they're doing it on purpose. Like they're leaving those little signs to prove I'm messing up, just building this whole case to get me fired. 

I really try to just brush it off, because like I said, my husband keeps telling me it’s just normal restaurant mess-ups and that everyone just has sloppy handwriting when it's busy. And I really want to believe him! I know he's probably right, and I'm trying so hard to see it his way so I don't cause any drama at work. I want to be a team player. But in the moment... it just feels so incredibly real to me. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds so paranoid and terrible. Am I... is it okay that I'm telling you all this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and answering what you actually need to know.
Even though your husband says it's just messy handwriting, do you still feel certain that these marks are intentionally placed to get you fired, or have you been able to doubt that idea at all?

Um... well... I mean, I really do try to doubt it. I try so, so hard to just listen to my husband, because he's so smart and level-headed. And I know it makes me sound awful to say I don't believe him. 

But... oh gosh, I hate admitting this... even when he tells me it's just messy handwriting and normal restaurant mistakes, I... I still just feel so certain about it. It's like, no matter how much I tell myself to just be normal and let it go, I still have this overwhelming feeling that those servers and that one customer are watching me ring things in. And those little signs on the tickets... it just feels so real that they're doing it to get me fired. 

I really am trying to stop thinking that way, I promise! I don't want to be the kind of person who thinks badly of their coworkers. I know I should just trust my husband... does it make me a really difficult patient that I can't just shake the feeling? I hope I'm not frustrating you by saying the same thing again... I just want to be totally honest so I'm doing this right.

Even though others have told you that the handwriting on the tickets is normal and that you’re not doing anything wrong, do you still feel completely certain that these marks are intentional and part of a plan to get you fired?

Um... yeah. I... I know I keep saying the same thing, and I'm really sorry if I'm being repetitive or... or stubborn. I don't want you to think I'm ignoring what everyone is telling me, because I really do listen! I listen to my husband, and I know he means well when he says it's just normal mess-ups. 

But... yes. To answer your question... I do still feel certain. It's just... when I'm there, standing at the computer, I still get that feeling that those servers and that regular customer are watching me ring things in. And those little signs on the tickets... I just can't shake the feeling that they're doing it on purpose to get me fired. 

I'm really trying not to let it affect my work, though! I still smile and do my best every shift. I just... I can't help but feel like it's real, even when I know I'm supposed to think otherwise. Is... is that okay to admit? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the honest truth, like you asked.

Even though your husband and others have clearly told you that the handwriting on the tickets is normal and that you’re not doing anything wrong, do you still feel completely convinced—without any doubt—that these markings are intentional and part of a plan to get you fired?

Um... I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm failing a test or something because you have to keep asking me. I really, really want to give you the right answer, and I know the normal thing to say is that I have doubts. I don't want to be stubborn! 

But... yes. I am. I'm completely convinced. Even with my husband telling me over and over that it's just normal restaurant mess-ups... I just can't turn off that feeling. I still feel like a couple of those servers and that one regular customer are watching exactly how I ring things in. And the little signs on the tickets... they're just too specific. I know in my heart they're doing it to prove I'm messing up so they can get me fired. 

I hope you're not mad at me for not changing my mind. I'm just trying to be a good patient and tell you the absolute truth, even when it's embarrassing to admit that I can't just listen to reason. Is... is that what you needed to know? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.

Even though your husband and others have clearly told you that the handwriting on the tickets is normal and that you’re not doing anything wrong, do you still feel completely convinced—without any doubt—that these markings are intentional and part of a plan to get you fired?

Oh, gosh... I'm so, so sorry, Doctor. I feel terrible that you have to keep asking me the exact same thing. I must be doing a really bad job of explaining myself, or... or maybe I'm just being a incredibly frustrating patient today. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult! 

But... yes. I don't have any doubt. Even though I really, really want to agree with my husband when he says it's just normal restaurant mess-ups... I still just keep feeling like a couple of the servers and that one regular customer are watching how I ring things in. And they're leaving those little signs on the tickets to prove they're trying to get me fired. 

I know I keep repeating myself, and I feel so embarrassed that I can't just let it go like a normal person... I just want to be totally cooperative and honest with you. Am I... am I giving you the right information? I really hope I'm not making you upset by sticking to this.

Even though your husband and others have clearly told you that the handwriting on the tickets is normal and that you’re not doing anything wrong, do you still feel completely convinced—without any doubt—that these markings are intentional and part of a plan to get you fired?

I... I feel like I'm just making you go in circles, and I am so, so sorry for that. I really am. I know it probably sounds like I'm not listening to you or to my husband, and I don't want you to think I'm just being totally unreasonable. I know I should probably just say that I have doubts, because that's what a normal person would say, right? 

But... I just can't lie to you. I want to be a good patient and do this right. Yes... I am still completely convinced. I just... I can't shake the feeling. I'm really trying my best to explain it, but I know it sounds bad. I hope you're not getting frustrated with me. I'm just trying to be as honest as I can... is that okay?

Even though your husband and others have clearly told you that the handwriting on the tickets is normal and that you’re not doing anything wrong, do you still feel completely convinced—without any doubt—that these markings are intentional and part of a plan to get you fired?

Oh, um... I'm so incredibly sorry, Doctor. I feel like I'm doing something wrong because you have to keep asking me the exact same question. I really, really want to be helpful and give you the answer you're looking for. I know it makes me sound stubborn or... or crazy to not just agree with everyone else. 

But to be completely honest with you... yes. I don't have any doubts. Even though my husband keeps reassuring me that it's just normal restaurant mess-ups, I just can't turn off this feeling. I still feel like a couple of the servers and that one regular customer are watching exactly how I ring things in. And those little signs on the tickets... I just know they're intentional, to prove I'm messing up so they can get me fired. 

I'm so sorry, I know I'm just repeating myself and I feel terrible if I'm frustrating you. I'm really trying to be a good patient and tell you the truth, even when it's hard to admit. Am I... am I doing okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

F41.9 (Unspecified Anxiety Disorder) is no longer considered due to the presence of delusions that are not better explained by an anxiety disorder.
